subject: ACME POC - evaluation plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC - evaluation plan & success criteria

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap and next steps so we have alignment. Great conversation; primary goals from Acme: improve customer support classification accuracy and reduce time-to-resolution for Tier 1 intents.

Summary / success criteria (proposed):
- Intent accuracy (top intent) on Acme labeled set >= 92% (primary)
- Latency p95 < 300ms for inference in your EU region (secondary)
- Hallucination rate < 1% on a 200-sample manual check (safety)
- Integration and data controls: no customer PII persisted; logs masked per your requirements

POC scope and timeline:
- 4-week trial window (target start: week of Aug 2)
- Week 1: offline eval on labeled dataset + rubric setup
- Week 2: shadow deployment (online shadowing) to collect production inputs/metrics
- Week 3: iterate model config and rerun evals
- Week 4: run final pass, compile report and go/no-go recommendation

Ownership / asks:
- Marissa (me): overall POC lead, coordinate deliverables and weekly check-ins
- Rachel: draft evaluation rubric and selected labeled test sets (can you take point?)
- Dylan: infra/setup — configure sandbox, shadow endpoint, and cost estimate
- Acme: provide sample labeled set (ideally ~2k rows) and approve kick-off date

Attachments: acme-eval-plan-v1.xlsx (POC schedule + sample test matrix), redwood-poc-sla-draft.pdf (template)

Next immediate steps:
1) Samantha / Evan to confirm acceptance of success criteria and availability for Aug 2 start
2) Acme to share sample labeled data and any compliance checklist items
3) Rachel / Dylan and I to sync on rubric and infra setup by Fri 7/17

Thanks — happy to adjust any of the above.

Best,

Subject: Fwd: ACME POC - evaluation plan & success criteria

Rachel / Dylan — forwarding Acme's confirmation. High level asks for the rubric and approach:

Proposed eval methodology (hybrid):
1) Offline evaluation (deterministic): run Redwood model variants on Acme's labeled set to compute: accuracy, per-intent precision/recall, confusion matrix, hallucination markers (false facts), and tokenized cost estimate. This gives a quick quantitative baseline.
2) Online shadowing (production-like): shadow traffic for 1 week to capture latency, failure modes, and real input distribution. Run the same automated checks plus human review on a sampled subset (~200).

Why hybrid: offline gives reproducible, fast comparatives; shadowing surfaces real-world distribution and integration issues. We should weight both in final decision (suggest 60% offline / 40% online for reporting).

Rubric items to include (initial list):
- Overall intent accuracy (weighted)
- Per-key-intent thresholds (pass/fail)
- Latency p95 and error rate
- Hallucination / safety incidents per 1k responses
- Failure-to-classify rate (fallbacks to generic intents)
- Cost per 1k tokens (estimated)

Rachel: can you draft a one-page rubric with scoring bands (Green / Yellow / Red) and examples of manual labeling instructions?
Dylan: once Rachel drops the rubric, please spin up a sandbox project and a shadow endpoint; estimate expected infra cost for 1-week shadowing and send to me + Samantha.

I'll keep Acme looped for approval.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks — taking point on the rubric. Draft attached (eval-rubric-v0.md) and pasted highlights below. I aimed for actionable bands so Acme's reviewers can apply consistently.

Draft scoring (per test slice):
- Green (Pass): >= 92% overall accuracy; per-key-intent >= 90%; latency p95 < 300ms; hallucination rate < 1 per 1k samples
- Yellow (Caution): 85-92% overall; per-key-intent 80-90%; latency p95 300-500ms; hallucination 1-3 per 1k
- Red (Fail): <85% overall; any per-key-intent <80%; latency p95 >500ms; hallucination >3 per 1k

Manual review guidance:
- Use a shared spreadsheet (column: input, model_output, expected_intent, notes)
- Labelers should mark hallucinations when the model returns factually incorrect assertions about the customer or product
- For ambiguous cases, mark as "needs discussion" and we'll adjudicate with Acme SMEs

Weighting proposal: Offline metrics 60%, Shadowing metrics 40%. I'll convert the rubric into a scoring sheet so we can compute a final pass/fail and a recommendation.

I'll drop the markdown to the shared Drive folder and ping you when it's up.

-Rachel
